Analytical records: samples, injections, channels, and curves

Source: vignettes/analytical-records.Rmd
analytical-records.Rmd
library(measure)
library(dplyr)
library(recipes)

Record grain

A measure_record connects four practical levels:

Table One row represents Key relationship
samples One specimen or prepared sample sample_id
injections One acquisition of a sample sample_id links to samples
channels One declared detector stream channel_id; its name is a label
curves One curve in an injection/channel pair Links to both IDs

A reinjection gets its own injection_id and still points to the same sample_id. The .measures column is a measure_list, with one one-dimensional measure_tbl per curve. It can have a different number of points, grid spacing, or direction from another curve. In version 1, an injection has at most one curve per channel.

Map an interleaved long table

The small table below has two samples, two detector channels, and three injections. inj-02 is a reinjection of sample 0007. Rows from four curves are interleaved; the curves have unequal grids, including a descending axis. The literal ID NA is text. A blank signal is an unknown measurement, and a blank unit is an unknown declaration.

long_data <- tibble::tribble(
  ~sample, ~injection, ~channel, ~curve, ~channel_label, ~axis,
  ~axis_units, ~signal, ~signal_units, ~coordinate, ~response,
  "0007", "inj-01", "uv", "uv-01", "UV β, flow cell",
  "wavelength", "nm", "absorbance", "AU", 250.0, 0.12,
  "0007", "inj-01", "ri", "ri-01", "RI detector",
  "retention time", "min", "response", "RIU", 5.0, 1.20,
  "0007", "inj-02", "uv", "uv-02", "UV β, flow cell",
  "wavelength", "nm", "absorbance", "AU", 250.2, 0.21,
  "NA", "inj-03", "ri", "ri-02", "RI detector",
  "retention time", "min", "response", NA_character_, 0.0, 0.08,
  "0007", "inj-01", "uv", "uv-01", "UV β, flow cell",
  "wavelength", "nm", "absorbance", "AU", 251.0, NA_real_,
  "0007", "inj-01", "ri", "ri-01", "RI detector",
  "retention time", "min", "response", "RIU", 3.0, 1.10,
  "0007", "inj-02", "uv", "uv-02", "UV β, flow cell",
  "wavelength", "nm", "absorbance", "AU", 251.6, 0.18,
  "NA", "inj-03", "ri", "ri-02", "RI detector",
  "retention time", "min", "response", NA_character_, 1.5, 0.10,
  "0007", "inj-01", "uv", "uv-01", "UV β, flow cell",
  "wavelength", "nm", "absorbance", "AU", 253.0, 0.14,
  "0007", "inj-01", "ri", "ri-01", "RI detector",
  "retention time", "min", "response", "RIU", 0.0, 1.00,
  "0007", "inj-02", "uv", "uv-02", "UV β, flow cell",
  "wavelength", "nm", "absorbance", "AU", 252.7, 0.19
)

columns <- c(
  sample_id = "sample",
  injection_id = "injection",
  channel_id = "channel",
  curve_id = "curve",
  location = "coordinate",
  value = "response",
  channel_name = "channel_label",
  axis_name = "axis",
  axis_unit = "axis_units",
  value_name = "signal",
  value_unit = "signal_units"
)

Use measure_record_from_long() when the table is already in R. The mapping names are canonical record fields; the values are exact input column names. No identities or units are guessed.

prepared_record <- measure_record_from_long(
  data = long_data,
  columns = columns,
  source_id = "prepared-export-01"
)

prepared_record$curves |>
  select(curve_id, injection_id, channel_id, axis_unit, value_unit)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   curve_id injection_id channel_id axis_unit value_unit
#>   <chr>    <chr>        <chr>      <chr>     <chr>     
#> 1 uv-01    inj-01       uv         nm        AU        
#> 2 ri-01    inj-01       ri         min       RIU       
#> 3 uv-02    inj-02       uv         nm        AU        
#> 4 ri-02    inj-03       ri         min       NA

Read a CSV or TSV source

read_measure_record_delim() reads one local long table. Choose the delimiter and supply a source ID and column mapping. It retains text identifiers such as 0007 and NA, parses numeric fields with a fixed decimal point, and rejects unmapped columns unless allow_extra_columns = TRUE is set explicitly.

guide_dir <- tempfile("measure-record-guide-")
if (!dir.create(guide_dir)) {
  stop("Could not create the vignette's temporary directory.")
}
source_file <- file.path(guide_dir, "interleaved-curves.csv")

utils::write.table(
  long_data,
  file = source_file,
  sep = ",",
  row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = TRUE,
  quote = TRUE,
  qmethod = "double",
  na = "",
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
)

record <- read_measure_record_delim(
  file = source_file,
  columns = columns,
  source_id = "run-2026-11-11",
  delim = ","
)

stopifnot(
  identical(record$samples$sample_id, c("0007", "NA")),
  identical(record$injections$injection_id, c("inj-01", "inj-02", "inj-03")),
  identical(record$injections$sample_id, c("0007", "0007", "NA")),
  identical(record$curves$curve_id, c("uv-01", "ri-01", "uv-02", "ri-02")),
  identical(record$channels$channel_name[[1]], "UV β, flow cell"),
  identical(record$sources$source_name[[1]], basename(source_file)),
  grepl("^[0-9a-f]{64}$", record$sources$source_sha256[[1]]),
  is.na(record$curves$value_unit[[4]]),
  anyNA(record$curves$.measures[[1]]$value),
  is.na(prepared_record$sources$source_sha256[[1]])
)

record$sources
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   source_id      source_name            source_sha256                           
#>   <chr>          <chr>                  <chr>                                   
#> 1 run-2026-11-11 interleaved-curves.csv 2b62942cc7484f7a01ac9d3ad280e6fd47d3471…

The file reader records the input basename and a SHA-256 digest of the exact source bytes it parsed. The ID remains the caller’s declaration. The in-memory converter cannot hash original file bytes, so its source digest is missing.

.source_rows records each point’s 1-based parsed-record ordinal. These are logical CSV/TSV records, not physical text line numbers: a quoted field can contain a newline. Because the curves are interleaved, their references are not a single contiguous range.

record$channels
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   channel_id channel_name   
#>   <chr>      <chr>          
#> 1 uv         UV β, flow cell
#> 2 ri         RI detector

record$injections |>
  select(sample_id, injection_id)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   sample_id injection_id
#>   <chr>     <chr>       
#> 1 0007      inj-01      
#> 2 0007      inj-02      
#> 3 NA        inj-03

curve_index <- record$curves |>
  mutate(n_points = vapply(.measures, nrow, integer(1))) |>
  select(curve_id, injection_id, channel_id, axis_unit, value_unit, n_points) |>
  left_join(record$injections, by = "injection_id") |>
  select(sample_id, injection_id, channel_id, curve_id, axis_unit, value_unit, n_points)

stopifnot(identical(curve_index$n_points, c(3L, 3L, 3L, 2L)))
curve_index
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   sample_id injection_id channel_id curve_id axis_unit value_unit n_points
#>   <chr>     <chr>        <chr>      <chr>    <chr>     <chr>         <int>
#> 1 0007      inj-01       uv         uv-01    nm        AU                3
#> 2 0007      inj-01       ri         ri-01    min       RIU               3
#> 3 0007      inj-02       uv         uv-02    nm        AU                3
#> 4 NA        inj-03       ri         ri-02    min       NA                2

source_rows_for <- function(x, id) {
  x$curves$.source_rows[[match(id, x$curves$curve_id)]]
}

stopifnot(
  identical(source_rows_for(record, "uv-01"), c(1L, 5L, 9L)),
  identical(source_rows_for(record, "ri-01"), c(2L, 6L, 10L)),
  identical(source_rows_for(record, "uv-02"), c(3L, 7L, 11L)),
  identical(source_rows_for(record, "ri-02"), c(4L, 8L))
)

axis_unit and value_unit are declarations only. For example, nm, min, and RIU are retained as supplied; a missing unit stays missing. The record does not convert units or treat an unknown unit as dimensionless. Likewise, NA_real_ means an unknown signal observation, not zero, censoring, saturation, or a detection limit.

Write and read the native bundle

write_measure_record() writes a new directory in the fixed version 1 bundle format. It is distinct from reading or writing one delimited long table. The bundle contains a manifest and fixed CSV or TSV tables for sources, samples, injections, channels, curves, and points. The source file itself is not embedded.

bundle_dir <- file.path(guide_dir, "record-bundle")
write_measure_record(record, path = bundle_dir, delim = ",")
restored <- read_measure_record(bundle_dir, max_bytes = 10 * 1024^2)

stopifnot(identical(restored, record))

list.files(bundle_dir)
#> [1] "channels.csv"   "curves.csv"     "injections.csv" "manifest.dcf"  
#> [5] "points.csv"     "samples.csv"    "sources.csv"

The full-object check confirms exact roundtrip of values and missing positions, axes, IDs, units, source declarations, and logical row references. The bundle reader checks the fixed schema version and member digests; its default max_bytes is 100 MiB for the total bundle bytes read. The delimited-file reader has the same default for its one input file. Both readers enforce the limit while reading.

Use the curves in a recipe

The curves already contain measure_list payloads, so a recipe can use a channel-consistent selection directly. This example retains the two UV injections as separate rows and applies an existing sample-wise normalization step without a long-to-wide conversion.

uv_curves <- record$curves |>
  filter(channel_id == "uv")

uv_sample_ids <- record$injections$sample_id[
  match(uv_curves$injection_id, record$injections$injection_id)
]

recipe_data <- tibble::tibble(
  sample_id = uv_sample_ids,
  injection_id = uv_curves$injection_id,
  .measures = uv_curves$.measures
)
record_before_recipe <- record
original_locations <- lapply(
  recipe_data$.measures,
  function(curve) curve$location
)
original_missing <- lapply(
  recipe_data$.measures,
  function(curve) is.na(curve$value)
)

record_recipe <- recipes::recipe(~ ., data = recipe_data) |>
  recipes::update_role(sample_id, injection_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_measure_normalize_vector() |>
  recipes::prep()

processed_curves <- recipes::bake(record_recipe, new_data = NULL)
processed_curves
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   sample_id injection_id .measures
#>   <chr>     <chr>           <meas>
#> 1 0007      inj-01         [3 × 2]
#> 2 0007      inj-02         [3 × 2]

processed_locations <- lapply(
  processed_curves$.measures,
  function(curve) curve$location
)
processed_missing <- lapply(
  processed_curves$.measures,
  function(curve) is.na(curve$value)
)
normalized_norms <- vapply(
  processed_curves$.measures,
  function(curve) sqrt(sum(curve$value^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
  numeric(1)
)

stopifnot(
  identical(processed_locations, original_locations),
  identical(processed_missing, original_missing),
  all(is.finite(normalized_norms)),
  all(abs(normalized_norms - 1) < 1e-12),
  identical(record, record_before_recipe)
)

Keep the input record as the acquisition record. A recipe step returns derived curve data; arbitrary recipe transformations do not promise to retain the record’s units, source hashes, or source-row references.

Scope and limits

This interchange format covers scalar, one-dimensional curves. It does not represent full multidimensional measurements such as a DAD surface or an MS spectrum at every chromatographic point. It also does not encode uncertainty, censoring, saturation, or missingness reasons. Use the existing n-dimensional classes for nD payloads and retain additional scientific semantics separately until they have a defined schema.

The CSV and TSV files are machine-interchange text, not spreadsheet-safe exports; spreadsheet software may interpret formula-like text. A SHA-256 value can help identify accidental byte changes, but it is not authentication or proof of scientific provenance. The bundle uses a fixed schema version, rejects unsupported versions, and reads only its fixed member names.
